paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. Paul tells Timothy that in the last days terrible times will come, and then he lists what people will be like. He says they will be "lovers of themselves, lovers of money," and "lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God" (2 Timothy 3:1-2, 4). Notice how many of those are LOVERS, because this passage asks the baker what they love most.

Then comes the part that should make every one of us sit up straight. These people are "having a form of godliness but denying its power" (2 Timothy 3:5). That's a cookie box with a perfect gold bow, and you open it and it's crumbs. Paul also describes women who are always learning but never able to come to a knowledge of the truth (2 Timothy 3:6-7), so learning alone is not the goal, because it should bring the baker to the truth, and the truth should change the baker.

And listen, because Paul doesn't leave Timothy hanging. He says to "Turn away from such as these!" (2 Timothy 3:5), and he says of them, "they will not advance much further," because "their folly will be plain to everyone" (2 Timothy 3:9). Truth wins in the end, friend. So when a baker sees a loud, shiny faith with nothing inside, the answer is not panic: keep your own box full, stay close to the truth, and keep those ovens ready.
